verdict.rationale: Zapier documents issuing a per-server MCP connection token for an agent. Each server carries its own tool list, and Zapier advertises 'permissions you control' plus account-level restrictions, which gives coarse credential scoping. The docs do not describe fine-grained least-privilege scopes on the token itself. Missing for 10: documented per-credential scope definitions (e.g., read-only or per-action permissions), token expiry/rotation/revocation controls, scoped client-credentials for the SDK/API, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Connect any MCP client to Zapier MCP by creating a server and generating a connection token, then adding it as a Bearer header or query parameter.
